messages:
maria: quick follow-up on the smart-routing RFC — we need to decide how strict policy precedence should be when latency vs cost vs region conflict. link: https://redwood-internal/rfcs/123-smart-routing :thinking:
kevin: my take: explicit priority list on the policy object. lowest complexity and easiest to reason about. e.g. prefer region match > latency SLO > cost band.
sasha: is that safe for multi-tenant Dedicated customers? region preference can force expensive GPUs. we need hard caps per-customer.
jules: +1 to hard caps. also think about fallback chains — if primary route is unavailable, what do we try next? compatible model variant, then alternate region, then degrade quality.
kevin: agree on chain. but ordering should be mutable at runtime (no code deploy). runtime config is a requirement.
maria: we already have an RFC that suggests a policy schema. quick sketch of a runtime policy yaml:

```
# policy snippet
id: route-policy-quickstart
priority: ["region", "latency", "cost"]
region: ["us-west-2", "us-east-1"]
latency_slo_ms: 150
cost_band: "medium"
fallbacks:
  - type: model_variant
    variants: ["quantized", "fp16"]
  - type: region
    regions: ["us-east-1", "eu-west-1"]
```

maria: this is what I'm proposing as the canonical shape. comments?
sasha: schema looks fine. two questions: 1) where do we store per-tenant overrides? 2) how do we express "soft" constraints vs hard constraints?
kevin: store defaults in config service, tenant overrides in secrets+policy store. soft constraints -> score functions, not boolean. e.g. cost_penalty: 0.7, latency_weight: 1.2. runtime sums scores.
jules: scoring is powerful but introduces opaqueness. ops will ask why a request went to an expensive host. we need deterministic tie-breaker and decision trace. add a decision metadata blob to every request.
maria: agreed — include a decision trace header: X-Rdw-Routing-Trace with route_id, evaluated_scores, chosen_path. small example: `routeTrace: [{rule: "region", matched: true, score: 0.0}, {rule: "latency", matched: false, score: 12.3}]`
kevin: perf note: computing scores on every request is expensive. we should cache evaluated policy for a key derived from (tenant, model, request_shape) for short TTL (500ms-5s). that covers bursty traffic.
sasha: caching plus invalidate-on-deploy sounds good. but how do we handle sudden region-wide capacity loss? need immediate invalidation. maybe policy engine subscribes to capacity events.
jules: yes, capacity events -> policy invalidation. also we should fall back to pre-specified emergency routes defined per-tenant.
infra-bot: deploy pipeline: policy-service v0.9 rolled to canary in us-west-2 (sha: abc123) — health ok :white_check_mark:
maria: thanks infra-bot. kevin, for the policy engine refactor path: do we want a layered approach? start with simple precedence + fallbacks, then add scoring engine in v2? keeps rollout safe.
kevin: layered approach makes sense. v1 = precedence + chain + traces. v2 = scoring + caching + ML-tuned weights.
sasha: interface boundary note: policy evaluation should be exposed as a read-only RPC (EvaluatePolicy) that other services call with a descriptor and get back a route decision + trace. don't couple callers to internal cache details.\nkevin: +1. EvaluatePolicy(tenant, model, request_profile) -> {route, trace, ttl_ms}. callers then honor TTL.
jules: long-term refactor: move policy authoring UI into Console and integrate with rollouts and canaries. need versioned policies, audit log, and rollback button.
maria: operational checklist for v1: add tenant hard caps, add decision trace header, store defaults in config service, runtime precedence config hot-reload, subscribe to capacity events, add small TTL cache. can we commit to that scope for next sprint?
sasha: yes if we drop scoring for now.
kevin: yes. I'll prototype EvaluatePolicy RPC and cache.
jules: ops will draft the emergency route template and SLA notes.
maria: awesome. I'll update the RFC with these follow-ups and a minimal YAML schema. final ask: everyone react with :thumbsup: if you approve the v1 scope. :rocket:
